project.name: Ezekiel
project.release_boundary: V1 frozen 2026-08-05. In scope: correctness and internal consistency of the three detection vectors and the decisions they drive; truthfulness of alert content; dashboard accuracy against the data it renders; data-integrity safety of compaction; documentation matching code. Out of scope: new detection vectors, external uptime monitoring (stated non-goal), profile_builder productisation, Twitter collection.

items.title: Product thesis and release boundary are explicit
items.value: Improvement remains aligned with the real product goal
items.acceptance: PRODUCT-INTENT.md identifies target users, critical journeys, intended identity, supported targets, V1 boundary, constraints and assumptions, with every product-defining contradiction either resolved or explicitly recorded.
items.notes: Four documentation/code contradictions found and recorded as C1-C4; all four resolved in code or docs.

items.title: A style-vetoed wallet cannot be promoted on ANY alert route
items.value: J2 — a false CRITICAL alert devalues every future alert
items.acceptance: Every code path that can send an alert about a candidate wallet consults thresholds.can_alert() (or a helper that does). Proven by source inspection of all alert call sites plus a regression test that fails if any route promotes a vetoed wallet.
items.notes: F-001 fixed. can_alert() is now reached from every alert route via combined_alert_ok(). Measured on live candidates: the tracer route would fire for 9 wallets instead of 29; the 20 suppressed are 15 style-vetoed and 5 score-decayed. Suppressed candidates keep their evidence. Verified by mutation: re-introducing this exact defect makes the suite fail, so the guard is real rather than a test asserting its own constants.

items.title: Match thresholds are decided in exactly one place
items.value: J1/J2/J3 — emails, scores, grading and dashboard must agree
items.acceptance: No module makes a behavioural-similarity promotion, corroboration or scoring decision using a hardcoded similarity constant. All such decisions derive from thresholds.resolve(). Proven by source inspection plus a test that a threshold change propagates to every consumer.
items.notes: F-002 fixed. No module compares a similarity score against a literal; risk.py, tracer.py and transfer_graph.py (3 sites) now resolve through thresholds.py. continuity.HIGH_CONFIDENCE_MIN was checked and deliberately left alone: it gates an aggregated continuity confidence, not a similarity score. Verified by mutation: re-introducing this exact defect makes the suite fail, so the guard is real rather than a test asserting its own constants. EVIDENCE ATTRIBUTION CORRECTED after the independent audit caught it: the runs labelled final-* were recorded at 7319d60dc/dbb8f350e, not a24d5ecf0 as this file and CHECKPOINT.md previously claimed, and some ran against a dirty tree. Superseded by the single atomic verification pass at the frozen commit recorded in FINAL-REPORT.md section 4.

items.title: The headline risk score reflects behavioural evidence proportionally
items.value: J3 — the single number the product exists to surface
items.acceptance: A behavioural candidate at the CONFIRMED tier contributes a substantial majority of the top_candidate weight, and a candidate at the proven self-match ceiling contributes full weight. Proven by unit test over the resolved thresholds.
items.notes: F-003 fixed. Was: CONFIRMED tier 2.91/22 pts, ceiling 4.17/22, max achievable 18.9%. Now anchored between the resolved gate and the proven ceiling. On live data the posture reads 40.5 not 26.1. Verified by mutation: re-introducing this exact defect makes the suite fail, so the guard is real rather than a test asserting its own constants. EVIDENCE ATTRIBUTION CORRECTED after the independent audit caught it: the runs labelled final-* were recorded at 7319d60dc/dbb8f350e, not a24d5ecf0 as this file and CHECKPOINT.md previously claimed, and some ran against a dirty tree. Superseded by the single atomic verification pass at the frozen commit recorded in FINAL-REPORT.md section 4. ALSO COVERS F-013, which FINDINGS.jsonl ties to this same acceptance ID and which this item previously failed to mention: the drawdown component of the same headline score was dead, not merely mis-scaled. collect_positions never published account/latest.json, so it held a portfolio payload (a list); both readers raise AttributeError on it and both swallowed it, pinning drawdown_pct at 0.0 and forfeiting a further 12 of the 100 points, while alert_account_value_drop never fired once. Fixed and pinned by six tests.

items.notes: F-004 fixed in all four consumers (tracer, risk, transfer_graph, dashboard). Live worst case was best 0.7113 / current 0.1322 still emailing as a behavioural match. items.title: Self-match validation passes and drives thresholds
items.value: J1 — an unvalidated scorer must not alert on behaviour alone
items.acceptance: src/backtest.py exits 0 with a PASS verdict against final HEAD, no dimension scores a hard 0.0, and the resolved policy published in scans/latest.json matches the report.
items.notes: F-010 fixed. This was a genuine live production outage of the primary detection vector, not a latent risk: live origin/main on 2026-08-05 had passed=false, self_score 0.45, rank 8, policy OBSERVING, behavioural alerting OFF. Local end-to-end after the fix: PASS, self-match 0.7461, rank 1/21, margin 0.1434, self_vetoes [], failures [], zero_dimensions []. LIMITATION: verified on local data through 2026-07-29; the production verdict on data through 2026-08-04 is decided by the next analyze.yml run. Verified by mutation: re-introducing this exact defect makes the suite fail, so the guard is real rather than a test asserting its own constants. items.title: Unrecoverable data is never destroyed by compaction
items.value: J5 — fills/funding/ledger/l1_transactions cannot be re-fetched
items.acceptance: compact_data.py cannot delete an archive source without reading the archive back and matching record counts, and never compacts the four unrecoverable datasets. Proven by source inspection and a dry-run.
items.notes: IRREPLACEABLE protects fills, funding, ledger, l1_transactions plus state, calibration, candidates; the archive is read back and record counts matched before any delete. Dry-run confirmed no changes and printed the protected list. Not re-verified under --apply: that mutates real, partly unrecoverable data.

items.title: No two systems decide the same outcome differently
items.value: Prevents the exact class of drift thresholds.py was created to end
items.acceptance: The 'fund-flow destination that also matches behaviourally' rule is implemented once and shared by scanner.py and tracer.py. Proven by source inspection and a shared test.
items.notes: F-005 fixed. Route selection and per-route thresholds are each defined once and shared by scanner.py and tracer.py. Scanner behaviour is unchanged by the refactor.

items.title: Dashboard critical journeys work in a real runtime
items.value: J3 — the operator's only visual surface
items.acceptance: Every route builds in the production configuration, and the data layer resolves real production data from raw.githubusercontent.com without error, returning correct values and degrading safely on null, empty and malformed input.
items.notes: Acceptance NARROWED from the original wording, which also required in-browser rendering and screenshots. Disclosed deliberately: no browser automation is available in this environment (Chrome extension not connected), so pixel rendering is split out as visual.dashboard-render. Verified here: all 7 live endpoints reachable, thresholds and policy resolve, topCandidate() correctly picks 0x12e16e (0.7019 now) over candidates[0] 0xcbd909 (best 0.7505, now 0.45), and every null/empty input returns a safe default. EVIDENCE ATTRIBUTION CORRECTED after the independent audit caught it: the runs labelled final-* were recorded at 7319d60dc/dbb8f350e, not a24d5ecf0 as this file and CHECKPOINT.md previously claimed, and some ran against a dirty tree. Superseded by the single atomic verification pass at the frozen commit recorded in FINAL-REPORT.md section 4.

items.title: Alert and dashboard content is factually accurate
items.value: J2 — trust is the product
items.acceptance: No alert body asserts a stronger claim than its evidence supports; tier names, thresholds and policy shown in the UI match the values used to alert.
items.notes: F-011 fixed. The banner, the recovery flow badge and the transfers page all now show the current score the backend actually graded on, so the displayed tier is the emailed tier as the README promises. NOT independently reviewed: the content-reviewer agent was not run. EVIDENCE ATTRIBUTION CORRECTED after the independent audit caught it: the runs labelled final-* were recorded at 7319d60dc/dbb8f350e, not a24d5ecf0 as this file and CHECKPOINT.md previously claimed, and some ran against a dirty tree. Superseded by the single atomic verification pass at the frozen commit recorded in FINAL-REPORT.md section 4. Extended: a tier badge now carries the caveat it needs. The scanner publishes a separation block - best_stranger, ceiling, margin, alert_headroom, confirmed_band and a THIN/MODERATE/STRONG grade - and each result shows where it sits between stranger territory and the target own self-match. On live data this exposes that the alert bar sits only 0.0665 above what a known stranger scores, that the confirmed band is 0.02 wide, and that a wallet labelled WEAK_LEAD at 0.4500 is in fact at 0.0% of range - indistinguishable from a stranger, which the label alone implied was a lead.

items.title: Rendered dashboard is clear, consistent and free of dead presentation
items.value: J3
items.acceptance: The production build emits no warnings, and no dead or silently-inactive styling remains in the files touched by this pass.
items.notes: F-009 fixed: .result-wallet a targeted an anchor that had moved inside <Addr>, where scoped CSS cannot reach it, so scanner addresses had silently lost their monospace styling. The build is now warning-free. Broader visual review is visual.dashboard-render.

items.title: Dashboard is operable and comprehensible without a mouse or colour
items.value: J3
items.acceptance: Critical journeys are operable without a mouse and comprehensible without colour: no positive tabindex, focus visible, every link has discernible text, charts carry a text alternative, status is conveyed by words as well as hue, and every text colour meets WCAG AA contrast on the worst surface it appears on. Agent-executed review, not certification.
evidence: scratchpad/a11y/*.html — post-hydration DOM from real Chrome, 6 routes
items.notes: UNBLOCKED, and three real defects were fixed to get here rather than the gate being waved through. (1) --text-muted was #555570 — 2.13:1 on a hovered card, below even the 3:1 large-text floor — while carrying the data-freshness indicator, chart axis labels and secondary table columns; --text-secondary was 4.43:1, marginally under AA. Both raised, with the luminance ordering preserved so the visual hierarchy is unchanged. (2) All nine chart canvases had no text alternative whatsoever; each now carries role="img" and an aria-label naming what it plots. (3) No explicit focus style existed — the UA ring was never removed, so focus was technically visible, but thin and low-contrast on a near-black page carrying 380+ wallet links; an explicit :focus-visible ring was added. Already sound before this pass and verified: h1 on every route, nav and main landmarks, zero positive tabindex, zero empty links, no unlabelled images, and status conveyed in words ("[WATCH]" on the banner, tier names on the scanner). SCOPE, stated plainly: this covers semantics, focus order, labelling, colour-independence and contrast maths on the built stylesheet. It does NOT include a screen-reader session, magnification testing, or testing with actual assistive-technology users, and it is not a certification. Two accent colours (--accent-red 4.27:1, --accent-purple 4.42:1) sit just under AA for body text and are used only for large numerals and badges, where AA-large applies.

items.title: No secret or unintended private data can reach the public repo
items.value: Repo must stay public for Pages/raw to work
items.acceptance: No credentials in code or data; alert code names missing env vars but never values; untracked local backups cannot be committed accidentally; dependency and injection risk reviewed.
items.notes: F-008 fixed (Ezekiel-backup-*/ gitignored). Checked and clean: no credentials in tracked files; all secrets read via os.environ and alerts.py names missing variables but never their values; workflows use only first-party actions/* with scoped permissions (contents: write only on data-committing jobs), no pull_request_target, no untrusted interpolation into run: blocks; the dashboard contains no {@html} so Svelte escaping applies throughout; emails are plain-text only (html_body has no caller). NOT independently reviewed: the security-reviewer agent failed on a session limit. Residual, not fixed: persist_candidate builds a filename from an API-supplied wallet string, judged effectively unreachable because a malformed address returns no fills and is never persisted.

items.title: Malformed, missing or partial data degrades gracefully
items.value: J1/J4 — the pipeline must not die on one bad file
items.acceptance: Missing/corrupt latest.json, absent credentials, and partial API responses are handled without crashing or silently asserting false state. Proven by adversarial tests.
items.notes: Two real defects found by probing, both fixed. (1) NaN survives json.load and compares False against everything, so max(0, min(1, nan)) returned 1.0 and a corrupt score earned the FULL 22-point risk weight, labelled "Behavioral candidate at nan%". (2) A list-shaped latest.json raised AttributeError past an except clause catching only (OSError, ValueError), killing the transfer-graph job; list-shaped latest.json files really do exist here (data/portfolio). NOT independently reviewed: the adversarial-tester agent failed on a session limit.

items.title: Jobs and dashboard stay within their budgets
items.value: Free-tier constraint is a product constraint
items.acceptance: Transfer-graph traversal respects its configured budgets; test suite and dashboard build complete well inside CI limits; no unbounded growth introduced.
items.notes: No regression introduced, and one avoided: build_graph resolves thresholds once and passes them to every node rather than the per-node disk read a naive fix would have caused across up to 300 nodes. Suite 369 tests in ~12s; dashboard build 100-165s; traversal budgets in config.json untouched. No independent performance review was run. items.title: Documentation describes the final product
items.value: The operator returns to this after weeks away
items.acceptance: README states the true test count and the true invariants; no documented guarantee is contradicted by code; stale architecture doc is corrected or clearly quarantined.
items.notes: F-006 fixed (156 -> 369). The stale ~0.54 self-match figure corrected. Added: the enforceable form of "only place thresholds are decided" with the three helpers to call; candidate_current_score for present-tense questions; the active-days rule and the live failure that motivated it; the SCORING_SCHEMA obligation; the absent dashboard test harness; and the one-cycle fingerprint key migration. F-007 (docs/architecture.md) left as-is: it already carries a staleness banner naming exactly the unbuilt components, and rewriting it sits outside this release boundary.

items.title: Independent release audit finds no unresolved blocker
items.value: The implementer must not be the sole judge
items.acceptance: A fresh read-only release auditor attempts to disprove readiness against final HEAD and reports no unresolved release blocker.
evidence: independent release audit of 2f816fcdd (verdict BLOCK, three process findings)
independent release audit of 33208e7c1 (verdict CONDITIONAL, no release blocker in code or behaviour)
independent verification of the discharge at ee7ab7a4d (all three conditions DISCHARGED)
items.notes: THREE independent audits ran, none by the agent that wrote the code. (1) Against 2f816fcdd: BLOCK. No code defect in the four vectors attacked; three process findings - the branch would not hold still because the mutation harness ran concurrently, evidence was attributed to commits it was not produced at, and RELEASE-MATRIX.csv was empty. All three accepted and fixed. (2) Against the frozen 33208e7c1: CONDITIONAL, stating plainly that no RELEASE BLOCKER was found in code or behaviour. It verified the freeze, ran pytest (375) and ruff (clean) itself, confirmed the certified runs record the right SHA with dirty false on both sides, and ran the carry-forward diff rather than trusting it. Its conditions were three documentation defects. (3) Against ee7ab7a4d, scoped to verifying that discharge independently: all three conditions reported DISCHARGED, each with the evidence used, plus independent re-confirmation of the evidence SHAs, the empty code-drift diff, the stopped preview servers, 375 passing tests and a clean ruff run. The earlier self-verification limitation is therefore RESOLVED. That third pass also found a defect the discharge had missed and in fact extended: FINDINGS.jsonl still marked F-001 to F-009 OPEN while every other document called them fixed, and the discharge commit had widened that sentence without touching the ledger. Corrected - the ledger now carries terminal statuses (13 FIXED, 1 CARRIED for F-007, which was deliberately not fixed), and the release-audit evidence record now asserts ledger/summary agreement on every run so the same drift cannot recur silently.

items.title: Rendered dashboard inspected in a real browser at representative viewports
items.value: J3
items.acceptance: Every route is rendered in a real browser against the production build and live production data, at desktop and mobile viewports, and inspected for hierarchy, spacing, responsive behaviour and page errors.
items.notes: UNBLOCKED. The Chrome extension was never connected, but Chrome itself is installed, so the production build was served with npm run preview and driven with headless Chrome directly. All 6 routes render at 1440x2400 and 390x2200 against live data: no route left loading text in the DOM, wallet addresses resolved (7 home / 371 scanner / 15 transfers / 13 recovery), and no page errors. The banner fix and the Margin Account Value / Portfolio Value relabel were both confirmed in the rendered pixels, not just in the DOM. Screenshots were inspected, not merely captured.
